title: A radio survey reveals megaparsec-scale diffuse emission around a cosmic-web node
summary: Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03. The team reports previously unnoticed diffuse radio emission extending about 5 Mpc and aligned with X-ray emission and galaxies; lensing supports a complex mass distribution with two low-mass systems on either side of the cluster. The authors propose that these systems are merging substructures in a massive cosmic-web node, while noting alternative interpretations remain possible.
ai_technology: Radio U-Net, a machine-learning detector for diffuse radio emission
organization: University of Bologna; INAF; University of Milano-Bicocca; National Central University, Taiwan; University of Tokyo; INAF Istituto di Radioastronomia; CINECA

evidence.tested: Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03.
evidence.unknown: The radio morphology and multiwavelength associations are reported observational results. The interpretation that the two faint components are subclusters merging with the central cluster is proposed rather than uniquely established; redshift/mass uncertainties and low radio resolution leave other emission classifications possible.
evidence.ai_role: Flagged diffuse low-surface-brightness radio emission in LoTSS data that had escaped prior human analysis, motivating the multiwavelength and weak-lensing study that characterized this new extended structure.
